body.statement: Using the unique-path centroid handle, determine the exact closed-form function \(Q_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) such that \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)=Q_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) for every feasible \(s\), and exhibit matching legal directed-tree transcript families.
body.justification: Unique component paths create a structured regime where exact rather than constant-factor counts should be attainable.
body.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional gives only the worst-case size of one local tree test, and GreenewaldKatzShanmugamEtAl2019CausalTrees treats one known tree skeleton.
body.consumer: The formula would provide an exact perturbation budget for heterogeneous arborescence models used as sparse regulatory-network approximations.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact closed form of \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) for arbitrary \(n\), \(K\), and every feasible \(s\).
obligation.obstruction: Unique component paths bound each local blocker set but do not determine how blockers for different heads and components can be batched in one adaptive target. No frozen result supplies a single legal tree baseline whose changed-target families certify the required global lower count.
obligation.attempted: Centroid path splitting, complement-singleton panels, and source-swap transcript alternatives were checked. They close the three-vertex two-component instance but do not yield matching counts for arbitrary path overlap patterns.
obligation.partial_result: For two directed trees on three vertices, the proved values are \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,1)=\infty\) and \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,2)=3\); complement-singleton panels also give an \(n\)-query upper bound when \(s=n-1\).
